sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:181888
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 3230 of 2022

Applicant :- Rahul Pandey
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Bhan Dubey,Anil Kumar Dubey,Kamta Prasad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajeev Kumar Pal,Sunil Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant in Court today is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri M. P. Yadav, Advocate holding brief of Shri Kamta Prasad, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned AGA for the State-respondent and Shri Sunil Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the informant.

3. The instant second bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.111 of 2020, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC & Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Machhalishahar, District Jaunpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 14.10.2020 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.28858 of 2020 and he is pressing the instant second bail application mainly on the ground that co-ordinate Bench of this Court while rejecting the first bail application has given a liberty to the applicant to renew his prayer for bail after recording the statement of the victim and during trial, as statement of the victim has already been recorded by the trial court, therefore, pursuant to the order dated 14.10.2020,
Rahul Pandey vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155891234/
1 applicant has moved the instant second bail application.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that applicant in the present matter is in jail since 03.07.2020 i.e. for more than three years and trial of the case could not be concluded till date and out of nineteen prosecution witnesses, only six prosecution witnesses could be examined and therefore, it appears that trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.
6.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted although as per the school record, the age of the victim was found around fourteen years but according to the doctor, in ossification test her age was found around sixteen years at the time of incident and as there can be a margin of two years either side, therefore, on the basis of radiological report of the victim, it cannot be said that victim was about fourteen years of age.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that as per the allegation, applicant dragged the victim and committed rape with her but in spite of that victim did not sustain any injury and this fact clearly suggests that allegation of rape made against the applicant is totally false.
8. Learned counsel for the applicant next submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.d on bail.

9. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and after considering the entire facts of the case, first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 14.10.2020 and according to the school record, victim was hardly fourteen years of age and as per the provisions of Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children)
Act, 2015, the educational age of the victim will prevail over her radiological report and therefore, it would not be appropriate for this Court to release the applicant on bail merely on the basis of his incarceration of three years and therefore, instant second bail application is liable to be dismissed.
10.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 14.10.2020 and at the time of rejection of his first bail application, the facts of the case were duly considered.

12. However, applicant in the present matter is in jail since03.07.2020 i.e. for more than three years but allegation against applicant is that he after dragging the victim, who is about fourteen years of age, committed rape with her, therefore, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail at this stage, accordingly the instant second bail application filed by the applicant - Rahul Pandey is rejected.

13. However, considering the fact that applicant is in jail since July, 2020 i.e. for more than three years, trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within a period of six months from the Rahul Pandey vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155891234/
2 date of production of a certified copy of this order strictly as per the provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C. and Section 35 POCSO Act, without granting any unnecessary adjournments to either of the parties, if there is no legal impediments.
